messages.text:
My mining pool account disappeared yesterday- mining worker is gone and my
15k bolts are gone. Can you help me restore it or do I have to set it up
all over again ?
Searched the web · mining pool "bolts" points worker account
Handed to the team · Pool account and Bolts balance live on the Harlo Pool backend; I cannot see or r

Note to the team: I looked into this. You'll need someone on our team for the 15,000 Bolts: they're stored on the Harlo Pool side, and I can't see or restore a pool account myself. I've passed your case to the team with everything you described. They're offline for the weekend and will pick it up …

Thanks for the info. Here is the info you requested:

BCH address: ····
Miner model: canaan avalon nano 3s
Last time Bolts were seen: 11/12 evening time

I won't set up a new account while I wait for the team on Monday. I'll
check my miner settings now.

Hi,

Thanks for sending those. Your BCH address, the Avalon Nano 3S and the timing (Bolts last seen on the evening of 11/12) are now in this thread, where the team will see them when they pick it up on Monday at 10am ET.

Here's how to check the Nano 3S. Open the pool settings, either in the Avalon Family app or by typing the miner's IP address into a browser on the same network. You're looking at three things.

First, Pool 1 should point to the Harlo Pool address you originally entered.

Second, the worker field should show your address exactly as you first typed it. The Nano 3S lets you choose whether to include the "bitcoincash:" prefix, so check whether you used it before. If the address looks different now, or the field is blank or reset, note what it shows before you change anything.

Third, look at Pool 2 and Pool 3. The Avalon switches to a backup pool on its own if it loses Pool 1. If a backup pool is set and the miner is mining there now, that would explain why your worker disappeared from Harlo Pool.

If anything doesn't match, put your usual Harlo Pool details back in Pool 1, save, and let the miner restart. Then reply with what you found, and a screenshot of the pool page if you can. Even if everything looks right, that's useful to know: it means the problem is on the pool side and not with your miner.

For a quicker answer over the weekend, try our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead).

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
